semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Both terms focus on the quantitative analysis of MRI data and are used interchangeably in literature.

parent_domains.justification: Quantitative MRI is a specialized application within the broader field of magnetic resonance imaging.
MRI, including quantitative MRI, is a subset within the broader category of medical imaging techniques.
Medical imaging, including MRI and its quantitative methods, fall under the general category of imaging techniques.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Being the direct field from which the quantitative methods are derived, magnetic resonance imaging is the most specific parent domain.

closest_child_domain.justification: There are no specific child domains listed under quantitative MRI in the provided list.

sibling_domains.justification: Diffusion MRI is another specialized form of MRI, similar to quantitative MRI in its specialization.
Functional MRI is also a specialized branch similar in specialization to quantitative MRI.
This is another application of MRI focusing on the brain, making it a sibling to quantitative MRI that also has specific applications in brain studies.
This is a different specialized application of MRI.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Both quantitative MRI and diffusion MRI focus on deriving additional information from standard MRI techniques.

unrelated_domains.justification: This is a broader domain that includes diagnostic processes and doesn't specifically relate to the quantitative aspects of MRI.
